# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45 (Bi-Vb Pc45)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc45  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45  
**Title (English, from literature):** Not resolving a legal issue  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45, titled *Adhikaraṇa* ("Not resolving a legal issue"), concerns an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) when a nun undertakes to resolve a legal issue but subsequently makes no effort to do so. As analyzed by Ute Hüsken, the rule was established to prevent nuns from rashly taking on obligations—specifically the settlement of a legal issue or dispute—which they subsequently cannot or will not fulfill, sharing a functional purpose with Pācittiya 79 [Hüsken 1997]. In the word-commentary (*padabhājana*), the text defines an *adhikaraṇa* by outlining the four standard types of legal issues: disputes (*vivādādhikaraṇa*), accusations (*anuvādādhikaraṇa*), offenses (*āpattādhikaraṇa*), and duties or formal acts (*kiccādhikaraṇa*), which the *Samantapāsādikā* notes is provided simply to illustrate the classification of legal matters [Hüsken 1997].
